## Paper and figure

Delavaux, C. S., Crowther, T. W., Bever, J. D., Weigelt, P., & Gora, E. M. (2024). Mutualisms weaken the latitudinal diversity gradient among oceanic islands. *Nature*, **627**, 335–339. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07110-y>.

**Figure 4** ([original](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10937366/figure/Fig4/)) compares pollination, mycorrhizal association, and nitrogen fixation. The top row shows mainland species richness; the bottom row shows each group's contribution to the island species deficit. I reproduce its points, curves, and standard-error bands with simulated data.

## Part 1: Infer the data

### Variables and observations

Species richness is a count. A group's contribution to the island deficit is its number of missing species divided by the total number missing across groups.

| Variable | Type | Simulated values or plausible range |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Identifier | Separate mainland and island identifiers |
| `latitude` | Continuous | Absolute latitude, 0–70 degrees |
| `type` | Categorical | Pollination, Mycorrhiza, N-fixation |
| `group` | Categorical | Biotic/Abiotic; AM/EM/NM; N-fixing/Non-N-fixing |
| `metric` | Categorical | Mainland richness or deficit contribution |
| `value` | Discrete count or continuous proportion | Nonnegative species counts, usually below 10,000; or proportions from 0 to 1 |

AM, EM, and NM denote arbuscular mycorrhizal, ectomycorrhizal, and non-mycorrhizal plants. I simulate 600 mainland and 212 island locations per group, giving seven groups and 5,684 observations across six panels.

### Generating data from the figure

Mainland latitudes follow U(0, 70). For islands, 204 latitudes follow U(0, 50) and eight follow U(50, 70), leaving fewer points at high latitudes. Locations are shared across groups. The tables give approximate mean values at ten-degree intervals; values between them are linearly interpolated.

| Group | 0° | 10° | 20° | 30° | 40° | 50° | 60° | 70° |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Biotic | 1250 | 1800 | 1450 | 900 | 700 | 800 | 450 | 150 |
| Abiotic | 15 | 20 | 30 | 50 | 110 | 170 | 150 | 50 |
| AM | 2100 | 3400 | 2800 | 2000 | 1500 | 1300 | 700 | 350 |
| EM | 10 | 15 | 25 | 40 | 80 | 140 | 100 | 40 |
| NM | 20 | 25 | 30 | 50 | 110 | 160 | 130 | 60 |
| N-fixing | 160 | 260 | 300 | 180 | 130 | 90 | 40 | 10 |
| Non-N-fixing | 160 | 200 | 180 | 170 | 290 | 410 | 260 | 120 |

For richness, add normal noise with SD equal to 70% of the interpolated mean, round, and replace negative counts with zero.

| Group | 0° | 10° | 20° | 30° | 40° | 50° | 60° | 70° |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Biotic | .98 | .98 | .96 | .93 | .85 | .75 | .63 | .50 |
| Abiotic | .02 | .02 | .04 | .07 | .15 | .25 | .37 | .50 |
| AM | .85 | .88 | .89 | .87 | .83 | .77 | .69 | .60 |
| EM | .015 | .020 | .020 | .025 | .030 | .040 | .060 | .080 |
| NM | .020 | .030 | .040 | .060 | .100 | .150 | .230 | .300 |
| N-fixing | .50 | .58 | .60 | .53 | .33 | .16 | .07 | .04 |
| Non-N-fixing | .50 | .42 | .40 | .47 | .67 | .84 | .93 | .96 |

For contributions, add U(−0.04, 0.04) noise and set a minimum of 0.001. Normalize within each location for pollination and N-fixation. The three mycorrhizal groups are not normalized because they exclude orchid mycorrhizal plants.

Biotic and AM richness peak at low latitudes, while non-N-fixing richness peaks later. Biotic and AM deficit contributions decrease with latitude; the N-fixation curves cross near the middle of the range.

### Simplifications

The numerical values are chosen by eye. I simulate mutualism types independently and generate deficit contributions directly, without reconstructing island inventories or matching richness totals across classifications. I omit spatial dependence and environmental covariates, and use `loess` instead of the paper's models.

## Part 2: Rebuild the figure

### Seeded simulation

```{r}
#| label: simulate
seed <- 5014
set.seed(seed)
library(ggplot2)
n_mainland <- 600
n_island <- 212
knots <- seq(0, 70, 10)
groups <- c("Biotic", "Abiotic", "AM", "EM", "NM", "N-fixing", "Non-N-fixing")
types <- c("Pollination", "Pollination", rep("Mycorrhiza", 3), rep("N-fixation", 2))
richness <- rbind(
  c(1250,1800,1450,900,700,800,450,150), c(15,20,30,50,110,170,150,50),
  c(2100,3400,2800,2000,1500,1300,700,350), c(10,15,25,40,80,140,100,40),
  c(20,25,30,50,110,160,130,60), c(160,260,300,180,130,90,40,10),
  c(160,200,180,170,290,410,260,120))
shares <- rbind(
  c(.98,.98,.96,.93,.85,.75,.63,.50), c(.02,.02,.04,.07,.15,.25,.37,.50),
  c(.85,.88,.89,.87,.83,.77,.69,.60), c(.015,.020,.020,.025,.030,.040,.060,.080),
  c(.020,.030,.040,.060,.100,.150,.230,.300), c(.50,.58,.60,.53,.33,.16,.07,.04),
  c(.50,.42,.40,.47,.67,.84,.93,.96))
latitude_mainland <- runif(n_mainland, 0, 70)
latitude_island <- c(runif(n_island - 8, 0, 50), runif(8, 50, 70))
dat <- data.frame()
for (j in seq_along(groups)) {
  mu <- approx(knots, richness[j, ], xout = latitude_mainland)$y
  share <- approx(knots, shares[j, ], xout = latitude_island)$y
  value <- c(pmax(0, round(rnorm(n_mainland, mu, 0.7 * mu))),
             pmax(0.001, share + runif(n_island, -0.04, 0.04)))
  dat <- rbind(dat, data.frame(
    id = c(seq_len(n_mainland), seq_len(n_island)),
    latitude = c(latitude_mainland, latitude_island),
    type = types[j], group = groups[j],
    metric = rep(c("richness", "contribution"), c(n_mainland, n_island)), value))
}
i <- dat$metric == "contribution" & dat$type != "Mycorrhiza"
dat$value[i] <- dat$value[i] / ave(dat$value[i], dat$id[i], dat$type[i], FUN = sum)
dat$panel <- factor(match(dat$type, unique(types)) + 3 * (dat$metric == "contribution"))
dat$group <- factor(dat$group, levels = groups)
panels <- levels(dat$panel)
```

### Smooth curves and standard errors

I fit a local regression for each group and metric. The bands show the fitted mean ±1 standard error.

```{r}
#| label: smooth-curves
curves <- data.frame()
for (g in groups) {
  for (m in c("richness", "contribution")) {
    z <- subset(dat, group == g & metric == m)
    model <- loess(value ~ latitude, data = z,
                   span = if (m == "richness" && z$type[1] == "Mycorrhiza") 0.50 else 0.40)
    grid <- data.frame(latitude = seq(min(z$latitude), max(z$latitude), length.out = 100))
    estimate <- predict(model, newdata = grid, se = TRUE)
    curves <- rbind(curves, data.frame(grid, panel = z$panel[1], group = g,
      value = estimate$fit, lower = estimate$fit - estimate$se.fit,
      upper = estimate$fit + estimate$se.fit))
  }
}
curves$panel <- factor(curves$panel, levels = panels)
curves$group <- factor(curves$group, levels = groups)
```

### Reconstructed figure

Points outside the plotted ranges are retained when fitting the curves.

```{r}
#| label: fig-reconstruction
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.8
palette <- c(Biotic = "#CC79A7", Abiotic = "#8A8A8A", AM = "#3B5BA5",
             EM = "#9BB4DE", NM = "#8A8A8A", "N-fixing" = "#6A9955",
             "Non-N-fixing" = "#8A8A8A")
limits <- c(2000, 4000, 700, 1.25, 1.25, 1.25)
legend_titles <- rep(c("Pollination syndrome", "Mycorrhizal type", "N-fixing type"), 2)
plots <- list()
for (k in seq_along(panels)) {
  z <- subset(dat, panel == panels[k])
  fit <- subset(curves, panel == panels[k])
  plots[[k]] <- ggplot(z, aes(latitude, value, color = group)) +
    geom_ribbon(data = fit,
                aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = group), alpha = .5, color = NA) +
    geom_point(alpha = .24, size = .65) +
    geom_line(data = fit, linewidth = .65) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 72), ylim = c(0, limits[k]), expand = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20, 40, 60)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = palette) + scale_fill_manual(values = palette, guide = "none") +
    labs(tag = c("a", "c", "e", "b", "d", "f")[k], color = legend_titles[k],
         x = if (k > 3) "Absolute latitude (degrees)" else NULL,
         y = if (k <= 3) "Species richness (species)" else "Contribution deficit (proportion)") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(legend.position = if (k <= 3) "none" else "inside",
          legend.position.inside = c(.98, .98), legend.justification = c(1, 1),
          legend.background = element_blank(), legend.key.height = grid::unit(.7, "lines"),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
          plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"), plot.tag.position = c(0, 1)) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, linewidth = 0, size = 1)))
}
p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 3)
p
```

::: {.figure-caption}
**Figure.** Simulated data for `r n_mainland` mainland and `r n_island` island locations per group: `r nrow(dat)` observations, `r length(groups)` groups, and `r nlevels(dat$panel)` panels. Lines are local regression fits; bands show ±`r 1` standard error. Seed: `r seed`.
:::

### Colorblindness check

Colors remain distinguishable within each panel under the three simulated forms of color vision deficiency below.

```{r}
#| label: fig-palette-check
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2.2
colors <- c("#CC79A7", "#8A8A8A", "#3B5BA5", "#9BB4DE", "#6A9955")
vision <- list(Original = identity, Protanopia = colorspace::protan,
               Deuteranopia = colorspace::deutan, Tritanopia = colorspace::tritan)
op <- par(mar = c(1, 9, 1, 1))
plot.new()
plot.window(xlim = c(0, length(colors)), ylim = c(0, 4))
for (i in seq_along(vision)) {
  rect(0:4, 4 - i, 1:5, 4.8 - i, col = vision[[i]](colors), border = NA)
  text(0, 4.4 - i, names(vision)[i], pos = 2, xpd = NA)
}
par(op)
```

## One improvement to the original

The original could use more distinct, colorblind-friendly colors for the mycorrhizal groups to make their overlapping curves easier to distinguish.
